title: The Bakery of Rosewater Lane
premise: Sebastian Marchetti, a jaded wedding planner who swore off love after her own engagement collapsed eleven years ago, discovers an undelivered letter in the walls of her late grandmother's bakery on Rosewater Lane — a letter she wrote and never sent, postmarked the week everything fell apart. Returning to the small vineyard town to sell the property, she is forced to plan one last wedding: that of her estranged sister, whose fiancé turns out to be connected to the man Sebastian abandoned. As harvest season ripens, Sebastian must confront the person she became after heartbreak, expose an old injustice committed against her grandmother's business partner, and choose between the safe life she's built and the vulnerable one still possible. She forgives herself, delivers the letter at last, and stays through the first harvest — not as a planner of other people's weddings, but as a woman willing to attend her own life.
about_author: Astrid Winterbourne is the pen name of a former pastry chef who spent a decade writing love letters for strangers before turning to fiction. She lives above a converted bakery, where she insists the ovens still warm the floorboards on cold nights.

chapters.title: Crumb and Ash
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In Boston, Sebastian flawlessly executes a society wedding while privately despising every vow she orchestrates. A call from a probate lawyer announces her grandmother's death and the crumbling bakery left to her. Emotional beat: grief disguised as competence; the crack in her armor begins.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Wall
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Arriving on Rosewater Lane to assess the bakery for sale, she pries loose a water-damaged wall panel and finds her own handwriting — an unsent letter from eleven years ago, addressed to Daniel, the man she left at the altar's edge. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past refuses its grave.

chapters.title: Flour on Her Hands
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Reading fragments of the letter, Sebastian relives the night she fled her own engagement and burned every bridge back home. Flashbacks interleave with her scrubbing the bakery, unable to leave yet unable to stay. Emotional beat: shame surfacing through muscle memory of dough and grief.

chapters.title: A Wedding in the Vineyard
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Her estranged sister Camille arrives unannounced with news: she's marrying Luca Ferro, son of the family whose orchards once shared the lane with Grandmother Rose's bakery — and she wants Sebastian to plan it. Emotional beat: resentment and longing tangled; duty knocks wearing love's face.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille admits she asked Sebastian knowing it would hurt, half-punishment, half-plea for reconciliation. They strike a brittle bargain: Sebastian plans the wedding, Camille helps restore the bakery until the sale closes. Emotional beat: two proud women negotiating tenderness through contracts.

chapters.title: The Ferro Family Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Researching venue logistics at the Ferro vineyard, Sebastian finds old account books showing Grandmother Rose was cheated decades ago — her partner, Luca's grandfather, quietly absorbed her share of the land. Emotional beat: righteous anger kindling; justice becomes personal.

chapters.title: Tasting Notes
chapters.summary: Luca's POV. Luca, the vineyard's winemaker, meets Sebastian over cake tastings and recognizes her name from his grandfather's guilty deathbed ramblings. Drawn to her despite what he suspects, he says nothing. Emotional beat: attraction shadowed by inherited debt; complicity begins.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian tracks down Daniel, now a teacher two towns over, intending only to return the letter. Their coffee goes wrong — old wounds reopen, and she learns he waited for her far longer than she knew. Emotional beat: the cost of cowardice made concrete.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Bakery restoration brings the sisters into rhythm: Camille bakes from Rose's recovered recipe cards while Sebastian repairs the shopfront. Camille confesses she resented being the one who stayed when Sebastian fled. Emotional beat: sibling wounds aired; forgiveness tentatively proofed like dough.

chapters.title: What the Vines Remember
chapters.summary: Luca's POV. Luca finds his grandfather's confession letter hidden in the cellar — full admission of how Rose's half of the vineyard was stolen. He must decide whether exposing it will destroy his family or free them. Emotional beat: dread and conscience wrestling in the dark among barrels.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. On the eve of first harvest, Sebastian and Luca work late planning the wedding and nearly cross a line both feel unready for. She glimpses the letter-shaped hole in him too. Emotional beat: intimacy as risk; two guarded people almost honest.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian finally reads the entire letter aloud alone in the bakery — an apology she wrote at twenty-four and never had courage to send. She realizes the letter wasn't really for Daniel; it was for herself. Emotional beat: catharsis; naming the thing she must forgive.

chapters.title: Ledger Day
chapters.summary: Luca's POV. Luca presents the confession and ledgers to his parents; his father threatens to disown him, his mother quietly produces documents proving she always suspected. Emotional beat: a family fracturing along fault lines of old sin; truth as inheritance.

chapters.title: Restitution
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Ferros offer restitution outside any court: Rose's name restored to the vineyard's founding label and the bakery's deed freed of the encumbrance that kept it unsellable. Sebastian realizes she no longer wants to sell. Emotional beat: justice without lawyers; grief transmuting into legacy.

chapters.title: Cold Oven
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille discovers Sebastian has secretly delayed the wedding planning, terrified that officiating joy will break her. Their fight is brutal — Camille calls her a coward who punishes everyone for one bad choice. Emotional beat: rock bottom; love spoken as accusation.

chapters.title: Daniel's Answer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian mails the letter at last, eleven years late, asking nothing. Daniel's reply arrives: gentle, final, forgiving — and closing the door. He married, has a daughter, wishes her well. Emotional beat: the past tense finally becoming past; freedom through release.

chapters.title: First Pressing
chapters.summary: Luca's POV. Harvest day. Luca asks Sebastian to co-sign the relabeled founding bottles bearing 'Marchetti & Ferro' and, haltingly, tells her he doesn't want to inherit his grandfather's silence. Emotional beat: courage modeled; an offer of partnership that means more than grapes.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The rehearsal dinner Sebastian planned unfolds beautifully — and she stands outside watching happiness she built but never believed in. Camille joins her, and they make peace under string lights. Emotional beat: standing at the threshold of one's own life; reconciliation sealed.

chapters.title: Vows
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The wedding day: rain threatens, the vines hold, and Camille and Luca exchange vows Sebastian wrote with her whole heart for the first time. Watching them, Sebastian understands belief isn't required to begin — only willingness. Emotional beat: climax of faith; love witnessed into possibility.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The morning after, Sebastian writes a second letter — this one to her younger self — and tucks it into the same wall cavity for whoever comes next. She signs the papers keeping the bakery, reopening it as Rosewater's again. Emotional beat: self-forgiveness completed; the mirror finally a friend.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Weeks later, the bakery reopens with Camille at the ovens and Sebastian planning events from the back room. Luca arrives with the first bottle labeled Marchetti & Ferro and an invitation to nothing more than dinner. She says yes. Emotional beat: quiet beginning; hope as daily practice.

chapters.title: Rosewater Lane, Evening
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Sebastian's POV. One year later: a wedding on the vineyard, a full case of founding-label wine, and a letter from a stranger found in the bakery wall thanking whoever left theirs. Sebastian adds a reply. Emotional beat: the circle closed and opened; love outlasting its letter.
